zh.title: 2026年還有哪些航空公司在經濟艙發盥洗包？
zh.summary: 2026年經濟艙免費盥洗包越來越少，只剩少數全服務航空公司在超長程或過夜航班上提供；阿提哈德、澳洲航空、阿聯酋與卡塔爾仍在特定航線發放，內容以實用與永續為主，成本與減塑壓力是背後主因。
body: 幾十年來，眼罩、襪子、牙刷與品牌收納袋是長途飛行體驗中一個小而貼心的點綴，但到了2026年，經濟艙免費盥洗包已越來越罕見，大致只剩超長程航線或少數想以此區隔產品的全服務航空公司還在提供。成本上升、乘客期望改變、拆分票價盛行，加上永續考量促使業者減少一次性用品，都是盥洗包退場的原因；許多航空公司現在只在旅客要求時才提供基本舒適用品，有的則全面改為機上販售。仍在發放的業者也把內容縮減為實用取向：阿提哈德航空只在約6小時以上的長程航班提供，裝在可重複使用的托特包裡，內容為降噪耳塞、眼罩與一小條護手霜；澳洲航空在部分長程國際航線提供，內容為牙科組、眼罩與耳塞，裝在以回收寶特瓶製成的裝飾氈布袋中，例如波音787-9執飛的伯斯—倫敦希斯洛直飛航線最長可達17小時；阿聯酋航空主要在長程、且多半是過夜航班提供，內容為襪子、眼罩、耳塞與牙科組，收在以回收聚酯纖維等永續材質製成的可重複使用收納袋中；卡塔爾航空在2026年的經濟艙盥洗包已不保證每班都有發放，多半只出現在特定的長程過夜航段。
盥洗包在經濟艙退場，不代表它從飛機上消失，而是兩端分化：高價艙等的盥洗包反而越來越講究，阿聯酋航空頭等與商務艙與寶格麗合作，卡塔爾航空與蒂普提克合作，新加坡航空頭等艙則曾採用萊儷等精品品牌產品。對旅客而言，現實是經濟艙的免費盥洗包已成為少數業者在特定航線上的差異化點綴，而非基本配備；若搭的是長程過夜航班，仍有機會拿到，但短程與日間航班上幾乎可以確定不會有。

en.title: The airlines still handing out amenity kits in economy class in 2026
en.summary: Complimentary amenity kits in economy are increasingly rare in 2026, surviving mainly on ultra-long-haul or overnight flights with a handful of full-service carriers; Etihad, Qantas, Emirates and Qatar Airways still offer them on selected routes, with practical, sustainability-minded contents.
body: For decades, eye masks, socks, toothbrushes and branded pouches were a small but thoughtful part of the long-haul flying experience. By 2026, complimentary amenity kits in economy are increasingly rare, largely confined to ultra-long-haul routes or a small group of full-service carriers seeking to differentiate their product. Rising costs, changing passenger expectations, unbundled fares and a stronger focus on cutting single-use products have all contributed to the decline, and many airlines now provide basic comfort items only on request or have removed them entirely in favour of buy-on-board options. The carriers that still hand them out have pared them back: Etihad Airways offers economy kits only on long-haul flights exceeding roughly six hours, in a reusable tote bag containing noise-cancelling earplugs, an eye shade and a small hand cream; Qantas offers kits on selected long-haul international routes, typically a dental kit, eye mask and earplugs in a decorative felt pouch made from recycled PET bottles, including its Perth-London Heathrow Boeing 787-9 service, which can reach up to 17 hours; Emirates still provides kits in economy primarily on long-haul services and often only on overnight flights, typically socks, an eye shade, earplugs and a dental kit in a reusable pouch made from sustainable materials such as recycled polyester; and Qatar Airways' economy kits are no longer guaranteed on every flight in 2026, tending to appear only on selected long overnight segments.

The amenity kit has not disappeared from aviation, it has split in two. In premium cabins, kits have become more luxurious, not less: Emirates works with Bvlgari in first and business class, Qatar Airways with Diptyque, and Singapore Airlines has offered Lalique products in first class. For economy passengers, the practical takeaway is that a free kit is now a differentiator offered by a few carriers on specific routes, not a standard inclusion; on a long overnight flight there is still a chance of receiving one, but on short or daytime sectors it is almost certainly absent.

facts.claim: In 2026, complimentary amenity kits in economy class are increasingly rare, largely confined to ultra-long-haul routes or a small group of full-service carriers.

Etihad Airways still hands out economy amenity kits only on long-haul flights exceeding roughly six hours, in a reusable tote bag containing noise-cancelling earplugs, an eye shade and a small hand cream.

Qantas offers economy amenity kits on selected long-haul international routes, typically a dental kit, eye mask and earplugs in a decorative felt pouch made from recycled PET bottles; its Perth-London Heathrow service, operated by the Boeing 787-9, can reach up to 17 hours.

Emirates still provides amenity kits in economy class primarily on long-haul services and often only on overnight flights; its kits typically include socks, an eye shade, earplugs and a dental kit in a reusable pouch made from sustainable materials.
In 2026, Qatar Airways' economy amenity kits are not guaranteed on every flight and now tend to be distributed only on selected long overnight segments.
Rising costs, unbundled fare models and sustainability efforts to reduce single-use plastics are driving the decline of economy amenity kits.
In premium cabins, Emirates works with Bvlgari, Qatar Airways with Diptyque, and Singapore Airlines has offered Lalique products in first class.
